name: Houari Boumediene Airport
before:
Algeria's main airport, 17 km east south east of Algiers.

The terminals need explaining because they have all moved around. Terminal 4 is the newest, opened in April 2019, and took Air Algérie's French routes first and then the rest. Terminal 1, the original international building, now splits into two halls: Hall 1 for domestic flights and Hall 2 for Middle East and Gulf carriers. Terminal 2 handles charter and pilgrimage traffic, with 20 check in desks, seven gates, a prayer room and 900 parking spaces. Terminal 3 is out of use and due to be demolished to make way for a new building, so check which terminal a client is flying from rather than relying on an older guide.

The airport is named after Houari Boumediene, a former president. In older writing about the Algerian War of Independence it appears as Maison Blanche, after the area it stands in.
after:
Algeria's main airport, about 12 km east south east of central Algiers in a straight line.

The terminals need explaining. International flights use Terminal 4, the West Terminal, which the airport's departures board shows as TO. Terminal 1 handles domestic flights and Umrah pilgrimage flights, and Terminal 2 charter and Hajj flights. There is no Terminal 3 in use, so check which terminal a client is flying from rather than relying on an older guide.

It stands in Dar El Beida, and its old name, Maison Blanche, still turns up in older writing.

claims.note: Air Algérie, the national airline, calls it the most important airport in Algeria and runs it as its connecting platform; Wikipedia calls it the main international airport of the capital. No national traffic table could be read (ENNA's statistics page answered 404). Wikipedia's infobox gives 9,151,517 passengers for 2024.

claims.note: Was '17 km east south east of Algiers'. Two position sets agree on about 12 km: OurAirports' airport with GeoNames' centre of Algiers gives 12.1 km at 111 degrees, and Wikipedia's own coordinates give 12.3 km at 112 degrees, which is east south east (112.5). The 17 km is Wikipedia's 9.1 nautical miles (16.9 km), from Algeria's aeronautical publication, measured from a point it does not name; it passes the coordinates check as a road distance, but no source gives it as one, so the straight-line figure is used, as at Guatemala City.

claims.claim: Air Algérie to Heathrow, Stansted and Manchester; UK traffic in 2025
claims.why: Held back: a new fact that replaces nothing. APS reported on 24 February 2026 that Air Algérie is adding Heathrow, Stansted and Manchester; the operator's board for 23 September 2026 has Air Algérie AH2056 to London Stansted from TO. The UK CAA's 2025 table counts passengers between Algiers and Heathrow (75,501), Gatwick (65,481) and Stansted (34,806, none in 2024).

claims.claim: Algeria closed its airspace to UAE-registered aircraft from 11 September 2026; UAE airlines' Algiers flights exempt only to 31 December 2026
claims.why: Held back, and on one source only, a trade news site (Aviation A2Z, 14 September 2026, which Wikipedia cites): Algeria cut diplomatic ties with the UAE and closed its airspace to UAE-registered aircraft from 11 September 2026, exempting UAE airlines' commercial flights to and from Algiers until 31 December 2026; Emirates' last Algiers flight had been expected in February 2027. APS's news index answered 500 (one try) and the FCDO's Algeria page does not mention it. Recommended for Andy: clients connecting through Dubai or Abu Dhabi may lose that routing from 2027. Needs a second source before it goes in.

quote: The restriction took effect at midnight on September 11, 2026, following Algeria’s decision to sever diplomatic relations with the UAE.
However, UAE commercial flights operating to and from Algiers Houari Boumediene Airport (ALG) have been temporarily exempted from the restriction until the end of 2026.

claims.claim: FCDO advises against all travel to within 30 km of Algeria's southern and eastern borders
claims.why: Held back: a warning that replaces nothing. The FCDO advises against all travel within 30 km of Algeria's borders with Libya, Mauritania, Mali, Niger and parts of Tunisia, and all but essential travel near the rest of the Tunisian border (updated 24 July 2026). Algiers is not in those areas.
